uncited: - **Sliding Interfaces**: Interior faces must be shared by exactly two tetrahedra.
- **Numerical Ambiguity**: Ambiguity at shared edges due to numerical issues can introduce holes or overlaps.
- **Zero Signs**: Any two (but not all three) signs $\sigma_{ij}$ may be zero.
- **Edge Orientation**: The sign of the permuted inner product changes if the edge direction is reversed.
- **When to Use**: When high-performance ray-tetrahedron intersection is required, especially in the context of tetrahedral mesh traversal where connectivity can be exploited.
- **When Not to Use**: When the mesh has sliding interfaces or when early parametric distance culling is critical and the overhead of post-processing is unacceptable.
The approach extends Garrity's grid-based traversal method [Gar90] and Wald's kd-tree implementation for initial tetrahedron search [Wal04].
